paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Nobody gets to walk into God's presence on their own résumé. Paul says Jews and Greeks alike are "all under sin" (Romans 3:9), and then he piles up the Scriptures until nobody is left standing: "There is no one righteous, not even one" (Romans 3:10). I looked for a loophole, I did, and I came up empty-mustached.

Now, that's not Paul being harsh for fun. He wants every excuse gone, so that "every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God" (Romans 3:19). And while the whole world's hands are empty, God stays true. Paul says, "Let God be true and every man a liar" (Romans 3:4), so even when people fall short, God's faithfulness doesn't fall with them.

So what's the law for, then? Paul says it "merely brings awareness of sin," and that "no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law" (Romans 3:20). It's a mirror, friend, not a washcloth. If you've been trying to scrub yourself clean to earn your spot, you can stop, because the mirror was never meant to do that job. The story isn't over, and the teaching isn't either, because Paul is about to show what God does about it.
